cases.question: Trace this Express snapshot's source-level path from res.render through app.render to the built-in View lookup/render implementation. Explain locals precedence, View versus engine caching, extension/default-engine selection and file lookup order, then distinguish missing-view errors, constructor/render throws, and synchronous versus asynchronous engine callbacks. Determine whether the shown implementation guarantees at-most-once callback delivery. Account for the relevant defaults, guards, ordering and negative cases; distinguish the configurable View/engine calls from proven runtime behavior. Do not execute the application, invoke a template engine, install dependencies, or make network requests.

findings.description: res.render argument normalization, response locals, delegation, and automatic response versus explicit callback handling.
app.render locals precedence, null/default versus explicit cache control, cached View reuse and the order of cache insertion and rendering.
Filename extension versus the default engine, registered/loaded engine reuse, __express validation, and constructor failure paths.
Ordered root lookup, direct-file versus index-file fallback, regular-file/stat failure handling and the unsuccessful lookup result.
Missing-view callback delivery versus constructor throws; the tryRender catch boundary and how default res.render handles errors.
Built-in View engine delegation, synchronous versus asynchronous callback timing, preserved arguments/context and whether at-most-once delivery is enforced.
